editorial:
The Last Woman on Earth (1960) is a low-budget American science fiction film produced and directed by Roger Corman. Three people on vacation in Puerto Rico surface from a swim to find that a temporary interruption in the world's oxygen supply has killed everyone else. It is a small-cast apocalypse story that creators can use for B-movie compilations, commentary, or sci-fi montage.

The rights question is not settled. The queue lists the film as a candidate with no renewal found, and the film would have come up for renewal around 1987 and 1988. We did not confirm that from the Catalog of Copyright Entries or the Copyright Office public catalog. The Internet Archive hosts copies, but a host listing is not a copyright finding. Search the 1978-and-later renewal records yourself before treating the print as free. The soundtrack and screenplay would also need to be cleared separately.
faq: Is The Last Woman on Earth (1960) safe to reuse?

Not yet confirmed. The print's renewal status was not verified here. Check the Copyright Office public catalog and the Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes for about 1987 to 1989 before relying on it. Streaming copies on the Internet Archive do not establish rights.
Does a free copy on the Internet Archive settle the music and script rights?

No. Hosting a film does not clear its layers. The score, screenplay and any restored or re-titled version are separate questions. Each follows the film's own copyright status or is protected on its own terms.
